title: Your leagues in the sidebar
body: The Leagues section of the sidebar now lists each league you play in this season, with your team, its win-draw-loss record and your next fixture, which opens its summary. Two dead links are gone: the Series chip on a tournament is plain text until series pages exist, and league registration settings now point to the Teams tab.

title: League announcements and fixtures table view
body: Organisers now post league news and message members from one Announcement button on the league header, and the dialog always posts to the season it was opened on. The Fixtures tab gains a round bar with Previous and Next, phase and team filters that reset per season, and a Cards or Table switch that the site remembers for you.

title: Site-wide restyle
body: The sign-in card, Account page, Standings, the tournament page and its Manage views, team pages, league settings, organiser tools and their dialogs, the match recorder setup and the smaller pages now share the same panels, tabs, buttons and tables as the Roster Builder and league page. Buttons that delete something use a strong scarlet fill so their labels stay readable.

title: NAF from your profile
body: When you register for a NAF-sanctioned tournament, the NAF name and number on your profile fill in automatically and go to the organisers, and you are told. If you have none you can add it to your profile on the spot, or declare that you are not a NAF member.

title: Organiser sharing and NAF-sanctioned registration
body: You now choose, per league and per tournament, which contact details its organisers may see; nothing is shared by default, and the Account page has a Sharing panel to change it. Organisers are told about every new registration, tournaments can be marked NAF-sanctioned, and your contact details take a country and at most one phone number.

title: Download and delete your data
body: The Account page has a Privacy panel: download everything the site holds about you as a ZIP file, or ask for your account to be deleted. Deleting keeps past results but shows them as a deleted coach instead of your name; deletion opens when the site goes live.

title: Portal mail
body: League organisers can message their members through the site without ever seeing an email address, and you control league email from the Email panel on the Account page. Every message honours your consent and unsubscribe choice at the moment it is sent; delivery starts when the site goes live.

title: Onboarding
body: After your first sign-in a Welcome dialog asks you to accept the privacy notice and set your preferred name and contact details; until then the site is read-only for you. Organisers see only what you choose to share, Discord ids are never shown to other coaches, and NAF details are edited only by tournament organisers for their own entrants.

title: Privacy notice
body: A public Privacy page explains what the site stores, why, how long it keeps it and how to reach us. It describes only features that are live today.

title: Match log order
body: The match log now reads from top to bottom, and the live feed follows the latest entry.

title: League header
body: The league page header shows the league name in the title font with its seasons badge and a Founded tag, and gains a Statistics tab. The season row now runs oldest to newest, and the chosen season stays selected as you move between tabs.

title: Light theme
body: The light theme is now derived from the dark one as soft greys, so both themes match. Switch with the sun and moon button at the foot of the sidebar.

title: Coach avatars
body: Upload your own coach avatar from the Account page; your Discord picture is the fallback. Result cards show the avatars of both coaches.

title: Free Create in the Roster Builder
body: A Free Create card replaces the BB2025 default ruleset, with an Ignore in-game limits option for building any team you like. Characteristic caps, the 8-skill limit and 16 players still apply, and shared Free Create teams show their builder prices.

title: Roster Builder redesign
body: The Tournament Builder is now the Roster Builder, with its Ruleset, Roster and Sheet steps in the page header. The Ruleset step shows rulesets and Pick a race side by side, the roster shows players as cards with a Team Captain badge and + Skill buttons, hire cards show cost and count at a glance, and accordion panels open in place.

title: New result cards
body: Past games show as result cards with both teams' colours, a big race crest with the race underneath, the competition under the score and room for coach avatars. The cards stack to fit the width of the page.

title: Welcome page for visitors
body: Visitors who are not signed in now see a League Manager welcome page with a short introduction, a sign-in button and recent games.

title: Sidebar and header refresh
body: The header has a Discord Login button and shows the page title next to the wordmark, gold on Tournaments and Leagues pages. The sidebar gains Browse Leagues, Build a team and Browse Tournaments buttons, a sun and moon theme switch, and a collapse tab at its bottom edge.

title: Sheet step previews the PDF
body: The Roster Builder's Sheet step now shows the exported team sheet on paper, exactly as the PDF prints it. The PDF gains a tournament ruleset box at the top right of the first page.

title: Page titles in the header
body: Each page's title now sits in the header bar instead of repeating at the top of the page, and the sidebar category names use the wordmark lettering.

title: Turn-by-turn log for online games
body: Game pages for games played on Super FUMBBL now show a turn-ordered match log, read once from each finished game's replay.

title: Roster Builder moves into the site
body: The team builder for tournaments now runs inside the site, with skills, stars and inducements on one pane and the roster, team controls and validator together on the Roster step. Old builder links take you to the new page.

title: Tournament Creator moves into the site
body: Organisers now edit tournament rulesets in the site's Tournament Creator, with tabs for the overview, tiers, team rules, skills, stars, inducements, advanced settings and a preview.

title: Create Tournament dialog
body: Organisers can start a new tournament from the Create Tournament button on the Tournaments page or from the account menu.

title: Game pages open the match report
body: A finished game's page now opens the match report in a read-only view with the full squads, fouls, winnings and league result details.

title: League team values recomputed
body: League team values are now worked out by the league from each player's stored value plus staff after every change, and the current team value leaves out players who miss the next game.

title: More detail from league games on Super FUMBBL
body: Results of league games played on Super FUMBBL now record whether a concession was legal, casualties suffered, attendance and extra player counters, and show them on the fixture summary, the game page and the roster. Slann teams and the Ball & Chain now build correctly for those games.

title: League statistics cards; rosters always visible; assign a coach to a team
body: The league statistics page now opens each rules edition (BB2020, BB2025, All time) with a row of spotlight cards: top scorer, casualty leader, most valuable player, best coach record, best team, biggest win, playmaker, interceptor, dirtiest player and iron man. Each card shows the big number, who holds it, their team and race with the race crest, the seasons it came from and anyone tied with them, and opens the player, the team or the match. On a phone the cards scroll sideways. The leader tables are still below. Team rosters are now always visible to everyone: the Hide team composition setting is gone. Redraft rookies never receive Team building starting skills, only the skills printed for their position. Organisers can assign a Super FUMBBL coach account to a league team from its roster on the Teams tab (for this season or every season of the team); the account is seated on the team’s fixtures that have no result yet, so a test league game can be played with it, and the change is logged on the season.

title: Result banking uses stored player values; no pre-game guard
body: A death, a missed game or a team-value adjustment now uses the player's stored value, which the fork team file carries from the league roster, and only prices skills when that value is absent. The fallback pricing is Primary skill 20,000, Secondary 40,000, Elite skill = the player's access price for its category + 10,000, with traits free and unknown skills still quarantining the result. The check that refused teams the banker could not price before a game is removed.

title: Leagues: overlapping seasons, news, Discord events, tier shortcut
body: A new season can now start while another is still in progress: the newest season becomes the current one, and Finish season lets organisers pick which open season to close. The Redraft board picks which finished season to redraft from and which season receives the draft lists (by default the newest finished season into the newest season in progress). League news is here: organisers post news on the league Overview (pin, edit, delete; simple formatting), the season’s coaches are notified, and the post goes to the league Discord. Organisers also get a fixtures editor on the Fixtures tab: add a fixture (home, away, round, date, or a test fixture), change its date, enter or clear the result, and delete one that has no result. Every Discord toggle is now wired: league news, fixture created, match started and match result post through the league webhook when switched on, with a [Test] tag on test fixtures. On the Team building tab, each roster row has Apply to all rosters in this tier, which copies its starting treasury and Primary, Secondary and Elite starting skills to every roster of the same tier (it asks first before overwriting values already set); save to keep them.

title: League fixtures can be played on Super FUMBBL
body: When a league plays on Super FUMBBL and an organiser allows a fixture, its summary page (Summary on any fixture in the Fixtures tab) now has Generate fixture on Super FUMBBL. Either coach or an organiser can press it: both league teams are built on Super FUMBBL from their league rosters (players, skills, injuries, SPP, staff and treasury as the league has them), the game is scheduled, the opponent is told "<Coach> has invited you to play your match on Super FUMBBL", and the organisers hear about it too. Pressing it again re-uses the same teams and game. Each coach then gets Start Game on Super FUMBBL, which downloads their own launch file; nobody else can take it. The page shows where things stand: teams built, game scheduled, in progress, result recorded, or failed with the reason, and organisers can reset a failed game (with a reason that goes in the history), allow a late launch, or cancel Super FUMBBL play for that fixture. When the game ends the result comes back by itself: the score, casualties and player lines go on the fixture, and both league teams are updated from the game the same way Super FUMBBL updates its own teams (SPP, injuries, deaths, missed games, winnings into the treasury, dedicated fans). Both coaches get a notification and the result posts to the league's Discord channel when that is switched on.

title: League redraft: board for organisers, re-hire flow for coaches
body: Start redraft in League settings now opens the Redraft board. Organisers see every team of the finished season, plus an Inactive tab for teams from earlier seasons that sat it out, with games played, wins, draws and losses, treasury and the redraft budget: the starting treasury, plus the treasury left, 20k per league game, 20k per win and 10k per draw, capped at 1,300k unless the league turns the cap off. Tick the teams to redraft (or Check all), override a budget with a reason, and Confirm redraft: each coach is told, and the league Discord hears about it. Coaches open their redraft from the notification or from their team page. First comes Rest and Relaxation: each niggling injury rolls off on a 4+, or a 3+ with an Apothecary, rolled by the site or entered from the tabletop; missed games clear. Then the Team Draft List: re-hire players at their value plus a 20k agent fee for every season they have played (players not re-hired retire), keep or drop rerolls, assistant coaches, cheerleaders and the Apothecary, hire new players from the roster, and watch the remaining budget as you go. The submitted list becomes the team for the next season, straight away if it has started or as soon as it does, and the organisers can follow progress on the board and close the redraft when it is done.

title: Match recorder: random seats, away team calls, Discord result summary, spectator view
body: Home and away are now drawn at random when a match is created (casual, tournament and test matches alike), and the draw is in the match log; an organiser can swap them before the first pre-game roll, which is logged too. The away team calls the coin toss, so there is no separate caller draw any more. When a match is confirmed, the final result (score, touchdown scorers, casualties, MVPs and any concession, with a link to the game page) is posted to Discord through the recorder webhook, marked [Test] for test matches. Anyone can now watch a match read-only at its recorder link: signed-in coaches who are not playing, and visitors for any match that is not a test match. Watchers see the scoreboard, the pre-game steps and cines as they happen and the match log, with no buttons, and the kick or receive choice shows as waiting for the coach who won the toss.

title: League settings: administration, information, registrations, team building, connections
body: League organisers and site admins now have a cog at the right end of the league header strip that opens League settings, in five tabs. Administration lists who runs the league (the owner, the organisers, who the owner adds or removes by coach name, and the site admins), starts a new season (numbered automatically, with its ruleset, carrying over the team building rules) and finishes the open season; Start redraft shows where the redraft board will go. Information holds the name, full name, description, default ruleset and where the league plays, with addresses checked for the United States (state and ZIP code) and Canada (province and postal code). Registrations sets which rosters may sign up, whether sign-up is open, hiding team composition and the limits per league and per race. Team building is a table of every roster with its tier, starting treasury and the extra starting skills the league grants (primary, secondary, elite), saved per season for the Tournament Team Builder to use. External connections downloads the results as spreadsheets (teams, fixtures, standings, participants, honours, awards), connects a Discord channel (the webhook address is kept private and only ever shown masked; a test post checks it) and turns on Play on Super FUMBBL, after which league admins can allow single fixtures, and both coaches and the organisers are told. The league name on the league page is now white and the logo sits centred in its strip.

title: Match recorder: pre-game fans, weather, inducements and coin flip
body: Every recorded match, test matches included, now walks the pre-game before Turn 1: the fans (D3 plus dedicated fans, with a short crowd cine), the weather (2D6 cine and a splash with what the weather does), journeymen, an inducement picker with prices, limits, petty cash and treasury, prayers to Nuffle, then the coin flip: the site draws which coach calls, everyone watches the coin land, and the winner picks Kick or Receive. Every roll can be made by the site (Roll for me) or typed in from the table (Enter result), and every step lands in the match log. Organisers can skip the pre-game (logged). Each milestone can also be posted to Discord for the BloodBowl bot when the recorder webhook is configured.

title: League players get stable ids
body: Every player in an imported league now has their own id, so two players who share a name are never mixed up. The id stays the same every time the league is re-imported, and the same player is linked across seasons (same team, shirt number, name and position), so career totals follow the player, not the name. Statistics leaders, the Honours boards and the roster rows all work from these ids, and a name in the leaders or an honours board opens that player's team with their row marked. When the TourPlay export lists two players of one team under the same name and position it still cannot say which of them earned the totals, so that total is shown once on the team and, in muted text, as a shared total on both players' rows.

title: Game pages: open any result for its summary and match report
body: Every card in Past Games now opens a page for that game. The result card sits at the top, followed by a summary: when it was played, the competition and round, casualties caused and suffered, any concession and the MVPs, plus each team’s scorers, casualty-makers and a player table when the game was played through the site (otherwise the page says per-player stats are recorded for games played through the site). Tabletop matches also show the match report: the key moments by half and turn, both teams’ finished-game summaries, and an Open match reporter button. Tournament fixtures link to the tournament’s Rounds tab.

title: Team sheet header: avatar click to upload, cleaner title row
body: The team sheet header is re-laid out: the avatar box on the left spans both rows, the team name takes the full width of the first row, and the second row has the race and special rules on the left with the coach name on the right (hover it for the last-updated date). The Team and On the fork status block and the Coach label are gone, on the share page too. On your own team page the avatar is now a button: hover or focus it and an Upload plate appears; click it to open the Team avatar dialog. On phones the avatar shrinks to 72 px and the name, rules and coach stack beneath it.

title: Leagues: TABBL with six seasons and all-time statistics
body: Leagues now have their own pages. TABBL, the Tahoma Area Blood Bowl League, is on the site with all six seasons: every fixture and score, the standings for each phase and division, each team's end-of-season roster with skills, SPP and the season's touchdowns, casualties and MVPs, the honour boards and the awards. The league page shows the Season 6 header bar with the TABBL logo, a Season picker (newest first, each marked BB2020 or BB2025), and tabs for Overview, Standings, Fixtures, Teams and Honours. The latest results show as wide result cards in the two teams' colours. A Statistics page adds career leaders, coach and team records, race win rates, biggest wins and champions, with a BB2020 / BB2025 / All time switch on top. League organisers can upload a logo and a header bar.

title: Mini calendar on the coach page
body: The Account box on the coach page is gone. In its place a Mini calendar shows the current month (Monday first, today outlined in green), a dot on every day with a deadline or fixture in that deadline's colour, previous and next month buttons, and an Upcoming list of your next five events from today onward, across months, each linking to its tournament or fixture. Full calendar opens the whole thing on the Account page. My teams now sits below it. Each team tile shows the competition it is registered in (or Not registered) and its current team value, and carries a red badge with the number of things still to do: advancement rolls waiting to be finished, players with an advancement they can afford, and roster problems flagged on a registration.

title: Sprite icons on the content panels
body: Every content box now carries a small pixel sprite before its title, in the same hand-drawn style as the sidebar: a newspaper for What's new, a hand bell for Notifications, an hourglass for Deadlines, a football for Recent games, two figures for Friends, a sealed envelope for Messages, a banner for My teams and a shield for Account. The Account page gets a nameplate (Identity), a calendar leaf, a chain link (Connections) and a clock (Set schedule); My teams, Leaderboards, Help, the tournament list and the tournament panels get theirs too. All original art, drawn for both the dark and the light theme.

title: Team avatar upload moved to the team page
body: The Avatars panel on My teams is gone. Open a team from My teams and use the new Team avatar button next to Share: it opens a dialog with the current avatar (or the race crest), a file picker, Upload and Remove. Pictures are cropped square and shrunk to fit, PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 512 KB. After you upload or remove, the team banner updates straight away and the dialog stays open. Teams that already have an avatar still show it on their My teams tile.

title: Team sheet totals: centred, bevelled, scoreboard numerals
body: The totals bar on the shared team sheet and the team management page now has centred, bevelled cells that sit lifted on a drop edge, with the values in the pixel heading font and the scoreboard's dark text shadow (TOTAL larger, keeping its tint). On the management page the Advancement column is now as narrow as its buttons (the header text is hidden but still read by screen readers), and the Add Skill / Add Stat buttons are bevelled and lifted: they rise on hover and press down on click.

title: Sidebar carets on the right; conceded games marked on result cards
body: Sidebar: the collapse caret now sits at the right end of each category header. Leaderboards and Help are plain links with no sub-list, and Testing Tools is now just Testing. Games: Recent games is now Past Games, a scrollable box of larger cards (two across on a wide screen) showing as many games as the server returns. A conceded game now says "Conceded by <coach>" and puts a red-framed plate behind its score; the struck-through team name is gone. Game cards are now bevelled panels that lift when you point at them. Team names such as <script>brains? no longer show as <script>: online-game results were stored with the fork's XML escaping and then escaped again by the page.

title: Connections: link and verify your NAF record
body: The Discord line on the Account page is now a Connections table: Discord, NAF and FUMBBL, each with a Linked / Not linked / Verified chip. Discord stays read-only: it is how you sign in. For the NAF, Link NAF account asks for your NAF coach name and number and checks them against your public NAF coach page; when both match the row turns Verified. The NAF has no sign-in or OAuth for other sites, so Verified means the record exists and matches what you entered, not proof that it is yours, and NAF sign-in is not possible. Re-verify checks again, Unlink removes the name and number, and editing either on your profile clears the check. Your FUMBBL name links through the FUMBBL name field, or shows as locked when tournament registration set it.

title: Recent games on the landing page
body: The page you see before signing in now shows the latest games played through the site, under the sign-in card, and the same strip closes the main column of your coach page. Each card shows both teams with their crests, races and coaches either side of the score, casualties in brackets under each number when they are known, and a tint of the two teams' colours. Tournament games say which tournament and round they belong to, tabletop games say Tabletop, and online games say Online. A tournament or tabletop card opens its page.

title: Sidebar polish: sprite icons, Resources, collapser in the top bar
body: The sidebar icons are redrawn as little retro game sprites: a house, a pennant, a trophy, a podium with a star, a question scroll, a treasure chest, a hammer, a rulebook, a television, a mountain shield and a globe, in greens, golds, browns and blues instead of all red. They are a little bigger too, and bigger again on the narrow rail. Useful resources is now just Resources. The button that folds the sidebar to the rail has moved up into the top bar, at the right edge of the sidebar; the [ key still does the same.

title: Set schedule from the calendar
body: The weekly availability editor is no longer a panel of its own on the Account page. The Calendar now has a Set schedule button beside Deadlines; it opens the editor in a dialog with your timezone, the seven day columns and Save availability. Saving reshades the calendar straight away. Close, Escape and a click outside close the dialog (a click outside is ignored while you have unsaved changes, and your edits are kept if you close and reopen). Links to /account#schedule open the dialog. On a phone the dialog fills the screen minus a small margin and scrolls inside.

title: New sidebar: Home, Leagues, Tournaments, Leaderboards, Help, resources
body: The left sidebar has a new layout. Home sits on top and still carries your unread badge. Below it come Leagues, Tournaments, Leaderboards and Help, each with its own pixel icon, and a Useful resources list linking Blood Bowl Base, Blood Bowl Dave, TABBL and FUMBBL in a new tab. Your own tournaments, teams and fixtures now sit under Tournaments. Every category folds open and shut with its arrow, and the sidebar remembers how you left it; Useful resources starts folded. On the narrow rail you see just the icons: click one to open the sidebar at that section. Leaderboards and Help are new pages: rankings arrive with league play. Account has moved to the menu under your name in the top bar.

title: Account page: identity, schedule and calendar
body: The Account page is rebuilt in the coach page style. Identity lets you set the display name other coaches see (it defaults to your coach name), your FUMBBL name and your NAF name and number; your avatar and the Discord account you sign in with are shown read-only. A FUMBBL name linked through tournament registration stays locked. Schedule is the weekly availability editor, unchanged. Calendar shows a month at a time, Monday first, with your registration and check-in deadlines, report-by deadlines and fixture deadlines as chips coloured like the Deadlines panel; each chip opens its tournament or match, and your usual availability is shaded on the matching days. On a phone the month becomes an agenda list. Proposed match times will appear here once that feature lands.

title: Player sheet on the team management page
body: Click a player on your team management page (the name in the table, or the top of the card on phones) and their player sheet pops out: number, position and sprite, the five characteristics with increases marked, printed, added and free Team Captain skills, SPP against the next advancement with a progress bar and the rank name under it, and the career stats the team file records: touchdowns, casualties caused, completions, interceptions, MVPs, fouls and niggling injuries, plus injuries and value with its breakdown (position cost + added). Stats are recorded for games played through the site; anything not recorded shows a dash, and games played are not tracked yet. Add Skill and Add Stat work from the sheet just like the row buttons. Escape closes it and focus goes back to the player.

title: Tournaments list in the site's design
body: The Tournaments page now looks like the rest of the site. The Active / Upcoming / Finished pills, which could stretch into tall capsules with a big empty gap above them, are replaced by a compact square switch next to the search box, right under the page title. It works with the keyboard too: arrow keys move between the three choices. Each tournament is a panel card with its banner (or the ruleset crest when there is none), a status chip, the dates (or Not set), ruleset, format, entrants and places left, and the round. The button at the bottom fits you: Manage for organisers, Your entry when you are registered, Register while places are open, otherwise Open. On a phone the cards stack in one column.

title: Simpler sidebar: Home carries the unread badge
body: The Coach page section is gone from the left sidebar: it was one page with a long list of links to itself. Home, in the Pages list, now carries a small badge instead. It shows your unread notifications (and, once they arrive, unread messages and proposed match times), updates as they come in, and disappears when there is nothing waiting. On the narrow rail the Home letter keeps a little count in its corner. The bell's list and the sections on the Home page are unchanged.

title: Tournament pages: banner, details and news
body: A tournament now has a front page of its own. Organisers can upload a banner (landscape, up to 1 MB), set the location, start time, entry fee, a summary and notes, registration and check-in deadlines, and post news; pinned posts stay on top. Text supports bold, italic, links and lists. Entrants get a notification when news is posted. The ruleset links open the Tournament Team Builder with the package preselected, and Edit ruleset opens the Tournament Creator.

title: Notifications from the bell
body: Tap the bell in the top bar and your latest notifications pop out right under it: the eight most recent, newest first, each with its icon, title, a one-line preview, how long ago it came and a dot while it is unread. Choosing one marks it read and takes you to it. Mark all read and a link to all your notifications sit at the bottom, and when there is nothing yet it says Nothing to read! Escape, tapping elsewhere or changing page closes it, and it works with the keyboard and on phones.

title: Team management page
body: Your team tiles on the coach page and on My teams now open a team management page laid out like the shared team view. For teams on the fork, each player shows SPP, rank and advancements, with Add Skill when they can afford a random or chosen Primary skill and Add Characteristic when they can afford the characteristic roll; random rolls are saved on the team until you pick. Tournament Builder sheets show read-only until the team plays on the fork. Share, Open in Tournament Builder and Back to My teams sit at the top. My teams now uses the coach page look, with avatars and build links in the side column.

title: Team Captain nomination in the team builders
body: Human, Orc and every other roster with the Team Captain special rule can now nominate a Team Captain in both the Team Builder and the Tournament Builder. Tap the round C beside a player to nominate them; picking another player moves the captaincy, and tapping it again clears it. Big Guys and Star Players cannot be captain, and the C never shows for rosters without the rule. The captain gains Pro for free: it adds nothing to skill cost or team value and never counts towards a tournament's skill limits. The nomination is optional, so the team summary shows "not nominated" as a hint rather than a problem. It is kept when you save, reload or share a team, prints on the roster sheet with a C marker and Pro, and the built team gives the game server both Team Captain and Pro. In a match, a team reroll used while the captain is on the pitch can come back free on a 6.

title: Coach page: What's new on top, availability editor fix
body: What's new now sits at the top of the coach page above Notifications. Editing a time in the weekly availability grid no longer re-sorts the column under your cursor; the blocks stay where they are until you save.

title: Notifications for coaches
body: Your coach page now has a Notifications panel, and the bell in the top bar shows how many you have not read. You get a notification when an organiser marks you paid, verifies or freezes your roster, checks you in or moves you to standby; when the roster check finds problems with your team; when a round is drawn and you have a fixture; and when a result you played is confirmed. Organisers hear when a coach withdraws. Organisers can also send you a message from the Participants table (Message coach), and it shows up here. Tap a notification to open the tournament, or use Mark all read.

title: Drag to reorder players in the Team Builder and Tournament Builder
body: Every roster row now has a gripper on the left. Drag a row with the mouse or a finger to reorder your players, or focus the gripper and press Alt+Up / Alt+Down. Player numbers follow the new order, and the printed sheet and PDF keep it too.

title: Easier-to-read recorder on the light theme and phones
body: Coach names use a darker green on the light theme so they read against the pale hero. On phones the Admin row stays folded behind the Admin chip until you tap it, giving the feed its height back.

title: NAF record line on the scoreboard
body: The match recorder's scoreboard shows each coach's NAF Glicko rating and W/T/L record, read from the coach's NAF page and refreshed when a fixture starts.

title: Coach titles by percentile
body: Coach titles now come from the coach's percentile in the active pool: Legend is the top 2 %, and a coach with fewer than 10 games is a Rookie.

title: Phone layout for the match recorder
body: The match recorder fits a 375 px phone: actions open in bottom sheets and every tap target is bigger.

title: Tournaments: submissions, roster lock, pairing, roles
body: Coaches submit a team and see whether it is valid; the opponent's team can be viewed; organisers lock rosters and start the event in one click, pair rounds with Dutch or Monrad, and run it from the Manage tab. Admins get a tournaments page.

title: Coach page and the new site navigation
body: A left navigation bar with League, Tournament and Coach page trees: your tournaments with their status, your registered team and whether it is valid, and your next fixture. It folds to a narrow icon rail (press [) and becomes a drawer on phones. The new Coach page gathers your deadlines (green, amber under 72 hours, scarlet under 24 hours, grey when overdue, shown in your timezone), your weekly availability on a 7-day grid, your teams, and this What's new list. Notifications, friends and messages arrive in the next lanes.
